To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified 60 novel human genes, whose products are related to the cell signaling/communication and nucleic acid management and are highly expressed in the human brain, and that these novel genes might be associated with the pathogenesis of brain diseases.
60 cDNA sequences of human brain genes were identified and their protein products were predicted.
we have isolated 60 new cDNAs which encode proteins of 733 amino acid residues on average and have annotated 25 of them as proteins related to cell signal transduction and nucleic acid management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of human cDNA sequences and their expression patterns.
the isolation, characterization, and expression analysis of human cDNAs which are predicted to encode large proteins.
the identification of novel genes and their expression profiles in human tissues, and will be helpful in elucidating their biological functions and the molecular mechanisms of human diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
25 genes are expressed in brain and that the functions of 21 gene products are known or predictable.
these genes are expressed in a tissue-specific or region-specific fashion in the human brain, and their products might be involved in the development of brain functions.
35 genes are likely to be expressed in brain and that the expression levels of the genes vary among brain regions and/or developmental stages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 60 cDNA sequences were deposited into the public database as KIAA1878-KIAA1937.

we have now completed the sequencing of cDNAs for 1,100 large human cDNA clones, which were selected from the cDNA libraries of human fetal brain, human adult whole brain, amygdala, placenta, and pancreas, in the present study.
the 1,500 genes analyzed in our project so far have been classified into the 12 functional groups: cell signaling/communication (28.7%), nucleic acid management (19.3%), cell structure/motil...
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human brain is an excellent source for the isolation of cDNAs encoding large proteins.
we were able to identify 25 novel human genes whose products are predicted to have functions related to cell signaling and nucleic acid management.
the human genome encodes a great number of genes which are related to the functions in cell signaling/communication and nucleic acid management.
